questions.question_text: A $0.15$ mole of pyridinium chloride has been added to $500\text{cm}^{3}$ of $0.2$ M pyridine solution (a base). Assuming there is no change in volume upon mixing(Given: $pK_{b}$ of pyridine = 8.82), the pH of the resulting solution is
questions.question_html: A $0.15$ mole of pyridinium chloride has been added to $500\text{cm}^{3}$ of $0.2$ M pyridine solution (a base). Assuming there is no change in volume upon mixing(Given: $pK_{b}$ of pyridine = 8.82), the pH of the resulting solution is
questions.explanation_text: Moles of pyridine present initially: $0.2 \times \frac{500}{1000}=0.1\text{mol}$ Moles of pyridinium chloride added: $0.15\text{mol}$ Pyridine is a weak base, and pyridinium chloride gives its conjugate acid, pyridinium ion. So the mixture acts as a basic buffer. For a basic buffer, $\text{pOH}=pK_{b}+log\frac{[\text{salt}]}{[\text{base}]}$ Since volume is the same for both, we can directly use moles: $\text{pOH}=8.82+log\frac{0.15}{0.10}$ $\text{pOH}=8.82+log(1.5)$ $log(1.5) \approx 0.18$ So, $\text{pOH}=8.82+0.18=9.00$ Now, $\text{pH}=14-\text{pOH}$ $\text{pH}=14-9=5$ So the pH of the resulting solution is $5$ Correct option: Option A.
questions.explanation_html:
Moles of pyridine present initially:

$0.2 \times \frac{500}{1000}=0.1\text{mol}$

Moles of pyridinium chloride added:

$0.15\text{mol}$

Pyridine is a weak base, and pyridinium chloride gives its conjugate acid, pyridinium ion. So the mixture acts as a basic buffer.

For a basic buffer,

$\text{pOH}=pK_{b}+log\frac{[\text{salt}]}{[\text{base}]}$

Since volume is the same for both, we can directly use moles:

$\text{pOH}=8.82+log\frac{0.15}{0.10}$

$\text{pOH}=8.82+log(1.5)$

$log(1.5) \approx 0.18$

So,

$\text{pOH}=8.82+0.18=9.00$

Now,

$\text{pH}=14-\text{pOH}$

$\text{pH}=14-9=5$

So the pH of the resulting solution is

$5$

Correct option: Option A.

$CaC_{2}O_{4}\longrightarrowCa_{S}^{2+}+\underset{S}{C_{2}O_{4}^{2-}}$

questions.question_text: Which among the following has highest $pH$ ?
questions.question_html: Which among the following has highest $pH$ ?
questions.explanation_text: For acidic medium, we know that $pH$ values range is between $0-6,9$ , for neutral it is 7 and for bases it is $7.1-14$ . So, $HCl$ is acidic and $NaOH$ is basic. Thus, we can straight forward infer that $NaOH$ has a higher $pH$ value. Now, 1 mole of sodium hydroxide produces 1 mole of $Na^{+}$ and 1 mole of $OH^{-}$ ions. This means that the concentration of the hydroxide ions will be equal to $[OH^{-}]=[NaOH]=1M$ For case A, $\begin{aligned} pOH & =-log[OH^{-}]=-log[1]=0 \\ \therefore pH & =14-pOH=14-0=14 \end{aligned}$ For case B, $\begin{aligned} [OH^{-}]=[NaOH]=0.1M \\ pOH=-log[0.1]=1 \\ \therefore pH=14-1=13 \end{aligned}$ So, $pH$ of $1MNaOH$ is highest among the given solution.
questions.explanation_html:
For acidic medium, we know that $pH$ values range is between $0-6,9$ , for neutral it is 7 and for bases it is $7.1-14$ . So, $HCl$ is acidic and $NaOH$ is basic. Thus, we can straight forward infer that $NaOH$ has a higher $pH$ value.

Now, 1 mole of sodium hydroxide produces 1 mole of $Na^{+}$ and 1 mole of $OH^{-}$ ions. This means that the concentration of the hydroxide ions will be equal to $[OH^{-}]=[NaOH]=1M$

For case A,

$\begin{aligned} pOH & =-log[OH^{-}]=-log[1]=0 \\ \therefore pH & =14-pOH=14-0=14 \end{aligned}$

For case B,

$\begin{aligned} [OH^{-}]=[NaOH]=0.1M \\ pOH=-log[0.1]=1 \\ \therefore pH=14-1=13 \end{aligned}$

So, $pH$ of $1MNaOH$ is highest among the given solution.

questions.question_text: $K_{a}$ values for acids $H_{2}SO_{3},HNO_{2},CH_{3}COOH$ and $HCN$ are respectively $13 \times 10^{-2},4 \times 10^{-4},1.8 \times 10^{-5}$ and $4 \times 10^{-10}$ , which of the above acids produces stronger conjugate base in aqueous solution?
questions.question_html: $K_{a}$ values for acids $H_{2}SO_{3},HNO_{2},CH_{3}COOH$ and $HCN$ are respectively $13 \times 10^{-2},4 \times 10^{-4},1.8 \times 10^{-5}$ and $4 \times 10^{-10}$ , which of the above acids produces stronger conjugate base in aqueous solution?
questions.explanation_text: Lower the value of $K_{a}$ , lower will be the acidic strength and stronger will be the conjugate.base. Therefore, among the given acids, HCN has the lowest $K_{a}$ value (i.e. $4 \times 10^{-10}$ ). Hence, it is the strongest conjugate base.

questions.explanation_html:
Solubility of AgCl is least in 0.1 M AlCl $_{3}$ reaction

Addition of $AlCl_{3}$ in $AgCl$ solution results in decreasing the concentration of $Cl^{-}$ ion. Due to the presence of common ion, the equilibrium shifts in the backward direction. Hence, the solubility decreases.
